newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean futures end mixed in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean futures end mixed in slow trade.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mixed in dull trading on Monday with investors remaining on the sidelines, traders said.
The key January 1997 contract ended at an intra-day low of 3,200 yuan ($385) per tonne, rising 100 yuan. It opened at 3,200 and hit a high of 3,230.
March fell 45 to 3,100, May rose 70 to 3,170, July fell 60 to 3,170, September 100 to 3,250 and November five to 3,360.
Combined volume was unchanged from last Friday's 10,400 tonnes.
Traders said many investors were not willing to build fresh positions with the coming of the Chinese lunar new year holiday.
"Investors do not want to build large positions at the moment, making soybeans lose direction," one trader said.
Traders expect soybeans to continue to move in a narrow range in the next few days.
